question: If a child is about to run into the street, what is an appropriate immediate response?
options: a:Start to prepare to slow down.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
note: If a pedestrian, especially a child, may enter the street in front of you, a sharp blast of the horn can warn them and help prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who reaches the intersection first.,b:The driver who reaches the intersection second.,c:The driver to your left should always be given the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, the driver who arrives first should proceed first. If multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After overtaking another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals you to return.,c:After signaling for three seconds.
note: Before returning to your driving lane, ensure there's enough room; seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror indicates adequate space.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the road, slow down and be prepared to stop; give them extra space and time to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.,b:Sound your horn as you begin to pass.,c:Flash your headlights as you pass.
note: Carefully judge the speed and distance of oncoming traffic to ensure you have enough space to pass safely on a two-lane road.

question: How can you help the driver behind you maintain a safe following distance?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early for turns, lane changes, and deceleration helps the driver behind maintain safe distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it before the light turns red; blocking intersections can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed through carefully.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow means prepare to stop. If you haven't entered the intersection, come to a safe stop unless stopping would be unsafe.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow, and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You are in a passing zone and may pass if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:You may only make right turns in this area.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass to the left when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When being passed, keep a steady speed and allow the passing vehicle to merge back safely.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Proceed through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.,b:Increase your speed to beat other traffic.,c:Adjust your mirrors before proceeding.
note: A steady green light permits you to go through the intersection, yielding to traffic and pedestrians already there.

question: When are large trucks most likely to lose speed?
options: a:When driving up long or steep hills.,b:When driving down long, gradual hills.,c:When driving in long, gradual curves.
note: Large trucks need more time to accelerate; they often lose speed ascending long or steep grades—give them extra space.

question: What is the 'golden rule' of driving?
options: a:Drive aggressively to get where you need to go.,b:Ignore other drivers on the roadway.,c:Treat other road users the way you want to be treated.
note: Treat other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians with respect and courtesy to help prevent conflicts and crashes.

question: When following a motorcycle, how should you adjust your spacing?
options: a:Allow extra space in front of the motorcycle.,b:Follow at the same distance you would a passenger vehicle.,c:Reduce following distance because motorcycles stop faster.
note: Give motorcycles more space because they can stop more quickly and are harder to see, especially at night.

question: If you are 21 or older, at what BAC are you in violation of the law?
options: a:0.08 percent,b:0.06 percent,c:0.04 percent
note: A BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers 21 and older and results in license suspension and possible criminal penalties.

question: When passing a pedestrian on the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.,c:Maintain steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
note: When multiple hazards are present, handle them one at a time—let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian if safe.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream; higher BAC indicates greater impairment.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Reduce your speed before a curve or intersection so you do not need to brake sharply while turning, which can cause a skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the roadway (onto the shoulder) to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not pass by driving off the paved road or onto the shoulder; this is illegal and unsafe.

question: What effect can combining prescription drugs with alcohol have on driving?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive.,b:It will likely have no effect.,c:It will make you more alert.
note: Many medications interact with alcohol to impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving unsafe.

question: If your vehicle experiences a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as safely possible.,b:Stop in your lane and put on hazard lights.,c:Signal and pull into the slow lane.
note: Get your vehicle off the road away from traffic and turn on emergency flashers so other drivers can see you.

question: Where should a 12-year-old sit in a vehicle equipped with airbags?
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:Any seat is acceptable.
note: Children under 14 must be secured in the rear seat using appropriate restraints to avoid airbag-related injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to take before making a turn?
options: a:Always move into the left lane.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Check traffic in all directions.
note: Before turning, check rear and both sides for traffic and adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.

question: On a highway, regularly looking far ahead of your vehicle will:
options: a:Allow you to spot upcoming police officers.,b:Help you keep up with traffic.,c:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.
note: Scanning far ahead helps you anticipate hazards, avoid sudden maneuvers, maintain steady traffic flow, and save fuel.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean regarding passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing across the centerline is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, what happens to your level of impairment?
options: a:You become more intoxicated.,b:You become more coordinated.,c:You become more sober.
note: BAC measures alcohol as a percentage of blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired a person is.

question: What are common consequences of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It can frustrate others and may result in a citation.,b:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,c:It cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating is dangerous, can provoke aggressive driving, and can lead to legal penalties for unsafe driving.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the proper immediate response?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly to slow down.,b:Apply the brake and hold it to stop immediately.,c:Pull over quickly without reducing speed first.
note: Keep control by holding the wheel firmly, gradually slow by easing off the gas and braking lightly, and pull off the road safely.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them toward the right (toward the edge of the road).,b:Keep them straight ahead.,c:Turn them toward the center of the road (left).
note: On roads without a curb, turn wheels right so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic without reason, what will likely happen?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic flow and possibly receive a citation.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You demonstrate proper defensive driving technique.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can obstruct normal traffic movement and may result in a ticket; match the flow when safe and legal.

question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which direction should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Toward the right, toward the side of the road.,c:Toward the left, toward the center of the road.
note: When parking facing downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Both directions may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and prohibit passing from both sides.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and it is safe to do so, move vehicles out of traffic to reduce the risk of additional collisions.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If possible, pull fully onto the shoulder, activate hazards, and remain in the vehicle until help arrives because walking along the interstate is dangerous.

question: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or white cane and is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield if at a corner.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way by drivers.

question: Which statement about driving while taking medications is correct?
options: a:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,b:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,c:Medications are safe to take at any time if prescribed by a doctor.
note: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can impair driving. Over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness; know how your medications affect you before driving.

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.
note: When leaving a driveway or alley, stop before entering the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians and traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before you slow and stop, scan your mirrors and surroundings so you are aware of traffic behind and beside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The vehicle across from your vehicle.,c:The driver on your left.
note: Vehicles proceed through a four-way stop in the order they arrive; if two arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does that indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic lanes where passing is not allowed for either direction.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the proper immediate action?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly to slow the car.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, take your foot off the accelerator, gently apply the brakes when safe, and steer to a safe location off the road.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway even when there is no marked crosswalk.

question: What is the only thing that will lower a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Drinking caffeine.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and reduce BAC; nothing else accelerates alcohol elimination.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, how must you respond?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely, unless directed otherwise by emergency personnel.

question: Which factors commonly contribute to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.
note: Speeding and driving too fast for road or weather conditions are major contributors to crashes; always drive at a safe speed.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Maintain your normal speed.
note: Slow down, obey posted speed limits, and be alert to changing conditions and workers in the area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Beep your horn.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your mirror, indicating adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after coming to a full stop?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to other traffic at the intersection.
note: You may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a complete stop and if no sign prohibits it and the way is clear.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large vehicles require extra turning space; wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn to avoid being squeezed or struck.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when is the correct time to start slowing?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane; then reduce speed to the ramp's advisory speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, at what speed should you be traveling?
options: a:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic speed.
note: Enter the freeway at about the same speed as traffic so you can merge smoothly; do not merge at a much lower speed than the flow.

question: When is it inappropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; it may confuse or startle them and reduce their safety.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to compete with them.
note: Avoid engaging aggressive drivers; safely yield or let them pass to reduce the chance of a confrontation or crash.

question: How does excessive speed typically affect driver behavior?
options: a:It often leads to high-risk decision-making.,b:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:It does not increase the chance of a crash.
note: Excessive speed commonly contributes to collisions by reducing reaction time and encouraging risky choices; it rarely saves time and increases crash severity.

question: When is the most hazardous time for turning or stopping on a rainy day?
options: a:One half hour after rain stops.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: When rain first begins, oils on the pavement mix with water and make surfaces especially slippery for the first 30 minutes.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the front wheels sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back on immediately.
note: Stay calm, slow gradually, check traffic, and when safe steer back on—abrupt steering can cause loss of control.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what size gap should you look for?
options: a:Four- to five-second gap in traffic.,b:Two- to three-second gap in traffic.,c:Three- to four-second gap in traffic.
note: Identify a four- to five-second gap before changing lanes so you have adequate space to merge safely.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass when which condition is met?
options: a:The vehicle ahead moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The yellow line next to your side is broken.,c:The opposite side's yellow line is broken.
note: If the yellow line next to your side is broken, drivers on your side may pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution; it does not require a full stop.

question: To check your vehicle's blind spots, what should you do?
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder into the blind spot.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Reduce speed and proceed through carefully.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon change to red; if you can stop safely, do so.

question: At a red traffic light that also displays a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:Be in the appropriate lane and the intersection is clear.,b:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Wait until the main light turns green.
note: If a green arrow is showing for your lane, you may proceed in that direction when the way is clear; yield to pedestrians and to vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have your lights on, which should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beams.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, use low beam headlights; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility in fog or precipitation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unlawful when attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Passing another vehicle in any marked no-passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: You may not pass in marked no-passing zones or over railroad crossings; both actions are illegal and dangerous.

question: What increased risk does fatigue while driving present?
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue impairs decision-making and reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel, risking serious crashes.

question: If the rear of your car begins to skid left, what should you do?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer to the left (in the direction you want the car to go).,c:Steer to the right.
note: If your vehicle skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go to regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's instructions?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only if children are present.
note: Drivers must obey crossing guards whenever they are directing traffic near schools.

question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.,b:Signal only and change lanes quickly.,c:Only check your mirrors.
note: Always signal your intent and check mirrors and blind spots to ensure the lane you plan to enter is clear.

question: When a large truck ahead is turning right on a multi-lane street, what might it do?
options: a:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.,c:May complete the turn in either lane.
note: Long vehicles often swing wide when turning because their rear wheels track a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Frequently check your rearview mirrors to stay aware of vehicles approaching and changes in traffic flow behind you.

question: In inclement weather, what is the recommended steering and braking technique?
options: a:Steer off the road.,b:Drive in a low gear.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In poor weather avoid abrupt steering and hard braking; smooth inputs help maintain traction and control.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a vehicle that cannot see behind it (trucks, buses, vans, trailers).,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a station wagon.
note: Increase following distance behind large vehicles that may not see you and that can block your view of the road ahead.

question: What is the nature of having a driver's license?
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state; it can be suspended or revoked for misuse or violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it legal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings permit passing.,b:Within the curve where you see no oncoming vehicles.,c:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.
note: Only pass where pavement markings and signs allow it; never pass in intersections or where your view is obstructed by curves or hills.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: The first half-hour of rainfall is most dangerous because accumulated oil and chemicals mix with water, creating slick surfaces.

question: How does driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic usually affect safety?
options: a:It is often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and attempt risky passes.,b:It is a good idea if the weather is bad.,c:It is appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can cause congestion and unsafe passing maneuvers by others; match traffic speed when safe and within limits.

question: If your vehicle is equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) and you need to stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Firmly press the brake pedal and hold it.,b:Pump the brake pedal repeatedly.,c:Gradually press the brake pedal.
note: When ABS is present, press the brake pedal firmly and hold it; the system will modulate braking to prevent wheel lockup.

question: If a school bus ahead of you in your lane has its red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Proceed after you think all children have left the bus.
note: When a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing; exceptions apply on divided highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when on a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you intend to go: on a one-way street a left turn should be made from the lane nearest the left curb.

question: What is the first driving-related ability alcohol affects?
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgment.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment, which is essential for making safe driving decisions and reacting appropriately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian who began crossing after the 'Don't Walk' started flashing is still in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian has crossed before proceeding.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian in the intersection; wait until they have cleared the roadway before moving.

question: If your car's suspension is failing, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: Faulty suspension reduces your ability to control the vehicle and causes excessive bouncing or difficulty steering; have it inspected and repaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are collisions more likely to occur?
options: a:When one vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,b:When all vehicles travel at the same speed.,c:When one lane travels faster than the others.
note: Crashes often happen when a vehicle's speed is out of sync with surrounding traffic—too fast or too slow relative to the flow.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: Avoid looking directly at blinding headlights; glance toward the right edge of the road and track the lane lines until the vehicle passes.

question: What is the main purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:To warn inattentive drivers by creating vibration and sound when a vehicle leaves the travel lane.,b:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they're leaving the travel lane or approaching a stop.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle in the lane.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, move it completely off the main-traveled portion of the road when it is safe to do so to avoid blocking traffic.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates what?
options: a:Traffic light ahead.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Do not pass.
note: Solid yellow lines on two-lane roads mark zones where passing is prohibited from the side with the solid line.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and allows passing on the left when no oncoming traffic is present.

question: As speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Looking well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turning on your headlights.,c:Changing lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds, stopping distance and reaction time increase—scan further ahead to detect hazards early.

question: At a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and also watch for multiple trains.,b:Only watch for trains.,c:Only watch for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
note: Approach railroad crossings cautiously. Be aware other vehicles (school buses, hazardous materials trucks) must stop, and multiple trains may be present.

question: When driving at night, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: Night driving reduces visibility—increase following distance and use high and low beams appropriately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,c:Approach in the lane nearest the right curb but move toward the middle before turning.
note: Approach the corner from the lane nearest the right curb, signal your intention, slow, and turn into the lane nearest the right curb on the street you enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before the turn is complete.
note: Continuous signaling informs drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians of your intended actions and helps prevent misunderstandings.

question: Facing a green signal while pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,c:Make pedestrians wait until you clear the intersection.
note: Drivers facing a green signal must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection and must yield when turning on a steady green.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When a broken yellow line is beside a solid yellow line, vehicles next to the broken line may pass; the solid-line side may not.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Both because children have less-developed reflexes and are smaller and harder to see.,b:Because they are always following traffic rules.,c:Because they can stop more quickly than adults.
note: Children are less predictable, have slower reflexes, and are harder to see; provide extra space and be alert near schools and parks.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Whenever you need to use them while moving.,c:Before you get into the car.
note: Adjust mirrors, seat, and safety belts before moving the vehicle so you're positioned to drive safely.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:In fog.,c:On a freeway at night.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist; high beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,b:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.
note: You must do everything reasonable to avoid striking pedestrians; yield when necessary even if they are crossing improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should match what speed?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic regardless of traffic speed.
note: When entering a freeway, accelerate on the ramp to reach a speed close to the flow of traffic to merge smoothly and safely.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions, impairing judgment and reflexes.

question: What should you expect when passing a row of parked vehicles?
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.,c:Assume other drivers and pedestrians will yield to you.
note: Maintain space from parked cars because doors may open or people or vehicles may appear suddenly between parked vehicles.

question: What does an orange and red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange-red triangle marks slow-moving vehicles like farm equipment, maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts.

question: If you come upon a flooded roadway ahead, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn around and find an alternate route.,b:Check the depth and cross carefully if it seems shallow.,c:Proceed without stopping.
note: Do not drive through flooded areas. Turn around and find another route to avoid water hazards.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.
note: Drivers must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until the bus moves again; this applies in both directions on undivided roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign you must give way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard; stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when it is safe.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and proceed when clear.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never drive through floodwater; it can hide hazards and may sweep vehicles away. Find an alternate route.

question: Why is night driving especially hazardous?
options: a:Because distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.,b:Because the speed limit is increased at night.,c:Because there are fewer cars on the road at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distances and speeds; your vision is limited to the range of your headlights.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is reduced, what should you do to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:Turn on your parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Turn up the instrument panel lights.
note: Use your headlights (low beams) in low light or when weather reduces visibility so other drivers can see you.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain posted speed to get through the water.,c:Shift into neutral while crossing.
note: Avoid deep puddles to prevent skidding and hidden hazards; do not drive through them if you can avoid them.

question: When driving in snow or ice, how should you make speed and direction changes?
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.,b:It is safe to use cruise control.,c:Drive as you would under normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual speed and steering changes and never use cruise control to avoid loss of control.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle equipped with airbags?
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat to avoid the danger posed by airbags deploying in the front seat.

question: Broken yellow lines on the pavement are used for what purpose?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions, and permit passing where dashed.
note: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic; dashed (broken) yellow lines indicate passing is permitted when safe.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is actively leading the person.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, cough syrups containing codeine or antihistamines (all of the above).,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs—including tranquilizers, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines—can impair driving.

question: What are so-called 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck to maneuver safely.,b:Areas with several car lengths between your vehicle and the truck.,c:Zones where you have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: 'No zones' are blind spots and areas so close to a truck that the truck driver cannot see or safely maneuver around your vehicle.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Have the pedestrian yield to you.,c:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.
note: Pedestrians who are blind or partially blind may use a cane or guide dog; you must yield and stop as needed to ensure their safety.

question: Which is the correct method for checking blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for left lane changes and over your right shoulder for right lane changes.,b:Only turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.,c:Vehicles with two mirrors have no blind spots so you need not check over your shoulder.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, then turn your head to check the blind spot on the side you intend to move to ensure the lane is clear.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can affect a driver's:
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time and can increase the risk of a crash.

question: What does a red-painted curb mean?
options: a:No parking, standing, or stopping.,b:Reserved for passenger pick-up and drop-off.,c:Loading zone only.
note: A red curb indicates you may not stop, stand, or park in that area.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked using only your rearview mirror.
note: Even with mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars and require extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror only.
note: Even with correctly adjusted mirrors, you must turn and glance over your shoulder to view areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Do not return to the lane until you can see the passed vehicle’s entire front in your rearview mirror, ensuring adequate space.

question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to finish the trip sooner.,c:Turn the radio up to stay awake.
note: If fatigued, stop in a safe location and rest; drowsiness greatly increases crash risk.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and given a citation.
note: You must have evidence of financial responsibility with you whenever you drive and show it to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

question: If a lane control sign over your lane shows an arrow with the word 'only', what must you do?
options: a:Travel only in the direction of the arrow.,b:Always make a lane change to reach your destination.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow instead.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and 'only' means that lane is restricted to the movement indicated by the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only return to the driving lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you not do?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself against the back of the seat.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: If struck from behind, keep your seat belt fastened and press your head into the head restraint to reduce whiplash; do not release the belt.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet road surfaces, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Make abrupt turns.
note: Decrease speed on wet roads to lower the risk of hydroplaning; if you lose control, ease off the gas and avoid hard braking.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you hydroplane or lose traction, ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel straight, and avoid braking until the tires regain traction.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross and you want to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes; wait until they have safely crossed before turning.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and continue driving.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: The safest response to fatigue is to stop and rest or switch drivers; short remedies like coffee or open windows are not reliable.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window regularly.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Regularly checking your rearview mirror helps you know how traffic is moving behind you and allows safer driving decisions.

question: If a vehicle approaches with its high beams on, what is the recommended initial response?
options: a:Quickly flash your headlights one time.,b:Do not dim your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights.
note: Flash your headlights once to remind the other driver to dim theirs; if they do not, avert your eyes to the right edge of the road.

question: A good driver should watch which areas around their vehicle?
options: a:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.,b:Only the middle of the road.,c:Directly in front of the car only.
note: To drive safely you must be aware of conditions around your vehicle—front, sides, and rear.

question: At what approximate speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at speeds just over 35 mph because tires cannot channel water effectively at higher speeds.

question: If you need to use your cell phone while driving, what is best?
options: a:Stop in a safe place first before using the phone.,b:Keep all phone conversations short.,c:Use a hands-free device and drive normally.
note: The safest option is to pull over and stop in a safe location before using your phone—distracted driving is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Merging into a different lane.,b:Slowing down.,c:Maintaining your speed and position.
note: If possible, move into the adjacent lane to create a gap for cars merging from the ramp; if you cannot, reduce speed to allow them to merge safely.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow for your lane, under what condition may you proceed?
options: a:If you are in the corresponding lane and the roadway is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only when the entire intersection is empty.
note: When a green arrow applies to your lane, you may proceed in that direction when it is safe, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: What actually reduces the effects of alcohol after several beers?
options: a:Waiting several hours for the body to metabolize it.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system. Coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed up metabolism; about one hour per drink is typical.

question: If parked facing uphill where there is no curb, after setting the parking brake which way should you turn the wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels to the right toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels left toward the center of the road.
note: Turning the wheels toward the road edge ensures the car will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams at night, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Straight ahead in the center of your lane.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping track of the oncoming vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, what is the safe procedure?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Slow down and just look both ways without stopping.
note: If cross traffic is obscured, come to a stop and move forward slowly until you can see clearly before proceeding.

question: When it is very foggy, which lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers only.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) in fog, mist, rain, or snow; high beams create glare and reduce visibility.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,b:Construction workers must yield to you.,c:You must yield to pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks; drivers must stop for them whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked, unless signals indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic but your light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Follow the vehicles ahead and enter the intersection.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it; blocking the intersection can lead to a ticket and obstruct cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When conditions permit, ease over or adjust speed to allow merging vehicles to enter safely and smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, you and the driver on your left arrive simultaneously. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your right (you have the right-of-way).,b:The driver on your left.,c:Whoever is signaling to turn.
note: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when clear.,b:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,c:Reduce speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match highway speed, signal, and merge smoothly into traffic when a safe gap appears.

question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicates what?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from that lane.,c:The protection of the green arrow is ending — prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protective turning phase is ending; you must yield to oncoming traffic if you proceed.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign at an intersection, what is required?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop: come to a full stop, yield to those with right-of-way, and proceed when safe.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stay focused on the centerline of the road.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming bright lights; glance toward the right edge of the road to reduce glare while still tracking the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If three vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: If vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed in arrival order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, drive in the right lanes unless passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic, use the right lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish right-of-way.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely through.,c:Enter and wait until traffic clears.
note: Even with a green light, do not enter unless you can clear the intersection before the light changes; don't block the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow warns that the protected turn phase is ending and you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic if you have not completed the turn.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your left foot for braking.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,c:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: Use your right foot to operate both accelerator and brake pedals, and apply brakes smoothly with increasing pressure.

question: Why should you not use high beam headlights when driving in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog, mist, or snow back toward the driver, creating glare and reducing visibility; use low beams instead.

question: What type of headlights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare and improve visibility in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can worsen glare.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination (all of the above).,b:Only reaction time.,c:Only coordination.
note: Substances like alcohol depress the nervous system and impair alertness, reaction time, and coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, how can you tell you have enough space to return to your lane?
options: a:You can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:If the other driver signals for you to return.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: Seeing the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror indicates you have sufficient space to safely return to your lane.

question: When driving through a work zone, what is the safest following practice?
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely to stay with traffic flow.,c:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible to avoid delays.
note: In work zones increase your following distance and do not tailgate; be prepared for abrupt stops or lane changes.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane at all times.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and allows lane changes when safe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by only looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Mirrors cannot show every area around your vehicle; large trucks have substantially larger blind spots than passenger cars.

question: How do you drive defensively?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.,b:Look only at the car directly in front of you.,c:Maintain just one car length of space ahead.
note: Defensive driving means scanning the road, checking mirrors, and anticipating hazards—not staring at one spot.

question: Do motorcycle operators have the right to use an entire traffic lane?
options: a:Use half of a traffic lane.,b:Use a complete traffic lane.,c:Use the shoulder of a roadway.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane and should not be passed within the same lane.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll into the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you should slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution; no full stop is required.

question: Why should you increase following distance when driving behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because other drivers always pull behind large vehicles before passing.,c:Because you'll be caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead and may not see you; increasing distance improves visibility and safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, at what point should you return to your original lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the passed vehicle's front bumper.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren and lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,b:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,c:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
note: If you are in the intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, clear the intersection and then pull to the right and stop to yield the right-of-way.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
note: Large trucks need extra stopping distance; leave space in front of them so the truck driver has room to slow and stop safely.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Allow time to calm down before driving; emotional distraction can greatly reduce your driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After signaling and matching the speed of traffic on an entrance ramp, what should you do before entering the interstate?
options: a:Merge carefully into the available gap in traffic.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the entire lane to clear before merging.
note: Accelerate to match traffic speed, signal, and merge into a safe gap; do not assume other drivers will create space for you.

question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Follow closer than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,b:Fall farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass immediately.
note: Large trucks have larger blind spots and require greater following distance for safety and visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At traffic speeds of 50–55 mph, how can you best reduce accident risk?
options: a:Stay within that speed range and adjust to the flow.,b:Drive a few mph faster than most vehicles.,c:Drive a few mph slower than most vehicles.
note: Traveling at a speed consistent with surrounding traffic (within posted limits) reduces crash risk from speed differentials.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure about your vehicle position?
options: a:Stay in the right lane as much as possible.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane; do not share a lane with them and ensure you are fully in the passing lane before returning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what is the appropriate manner to complete the pass?
options: a:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass as slowly as possible to remain beside it longer.
note: Execute a pass promptly and safely, then return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If you are being followed too closely (tailgated) on a two-lane road, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,c:Apply your brakes briefly, then resume your original speed.
note: If you are tailgated, slow down gradually or change lanes when safe so the tailgater can pass; don't speed up or brake-check.

question: How can sudden gusts of wind affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,b:They generally only affect very large vehicles.,c:They only create visibility problems.
note: Strong wind can create hazards for all drivers by reducing visibility (blowing dirt or dust) and by physically moving vehicles, especially light or high-profile ones.

question: If an oncoming driver's bright headlights bother you at night, what is the proper response?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look directly at the headlights to judge distance.
note: Avoid looking at oncoming high beams; instead glance toward the right road edge and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

question: Reaction time is slowed after:
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard all day.
note: Alcohol impairs reflexes, judgment, vision, and alertness, reducing reaction time and driving ability.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You should use cruise control to maintain a constant speed when approaching railroad tracks.,c:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.
note: Stop when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal; exercise caution near railroad tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a turn lane to make a left turn with oncoming traffic present, what should you do before arriving at the intersection?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be ready.,b:Signal in advance and keep your wheels straight until turning.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep your wheels straight until it is safe to begin the turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:If you increase your speed before the turn.,b:If traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:If traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic flows to the left, unless signage prohibits the turn.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:A motorcycle can stop more quickly than many vehicles.,b:Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as cars.,c:They always brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles can stop suddenly; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist brakes quickly.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what is allowed?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They must wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists often use the left lane when making a left turn; expect them to behave like other vehicles when turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires that drivers:
options: a:Be constantly alert.,b:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,c:Both of the above.
note: Safe interstate driving requires being alert and capable of handling higher speeds and traffic flow.

question: What color and lettering do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction and maintenance activities.

question: When entering a roundabout, whom should you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Only traffic already in the roundabout.,c:Only crossing pedestrians.
note: Yield to bicyclists and pedestrians crossing at the roundabout and to vehicles already circulating within it.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are legally considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous.
note: Bicycles on roadways are treated as vehicles; bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as motorists.

question: To be able to turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the wheel.
note: Place hands on opposite sides (commonly 9 and 3 or 8 and 4) for comfortable, quick, and controlled steering.

question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window to stay awake.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.
note: Stop and rest or switch drivers; short-term measures are not reliable substitutes for sleep.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address securely attached to the vehicle.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle or property, leave your contact information securely attached to it and report as required by law.

question: What is true about driving through roadwork zones?
options: a:Fines are the same as under normal traffic conditions.,b:You must 'Slow for the Cone Zone.' ,c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: Reduce speed and be prepared to slow or stop in work zones. Driving cautiously protects workers and other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, how should you enter an interstate?
options: a:Wait for a safe gap in traffic, then accelerate to merge.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up.,c:Use the shoulder to reach traffic speed.
note: On short ramps without acceleration lanes, identify a gap and then accelerate to match the speed of traffic before merging.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and allows passing when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning in wet conditions, what should you do?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads; reduce your speed to help prevent it.

question: The traditional mirror setting is:
options: a:May be appropriate for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight areas.,b:Appropriate for all vehicles in all situations.,c:Does not show the edge of the vehicle.
note: A traditional mirror setting (showing the vehicle edge) can be useful for trucks, vans, and SUVs when towing or backing in confined spaces.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, what should you do before going down steep hills?
options: a:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.,b:Maintain close following distance behind other vehicles.,c:Pump brakes continuously to keep them from freezing.
note: To prevent skidding, shift to a lower gear before descending steep hills and increase following distance. Pump brakes only if you lack ABS.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,b:Continue ahead because the motorist has the right-of-way.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they have cleared the roadway before proceeding.

question: If your tires begin to lose traction due to water on the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid applying the brakes.,b:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
note: If you hydroplane, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow naturally; do not brake suddenly, which can worsen the skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Assume all drivers automatically obey right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.
note: Never assume you have the right-of-way; be ready to yield if it helps prevent a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the likely effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time.,b:Helps maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious injury or death.
note: Excessive speed is a leading factor in crashes and greatly increases the severity of injuries.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How is a crosswalk defined?
options: a:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk is where pedestrians are intended to cross; it may be marked or unmarked and is protected by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
note: You must not pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; passing on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates what about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: Traffic in the lane adjacent to the broken yellow line may pass when safe; traffic next to the solid line may not cross to pass.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: What does a broken yellow line between lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line separating opposing traffic means passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle at all times.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always keep your eyes focused straight ahead.
note: Stay aware of surroundings—front, sides, and rear—to anticipate hazards and respond safely.

question: Which action is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Changing lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,c:Proceeding to the next exit if you miss yours.
note: Always signal before changing lanes; failing to do so is unsafe. Keep right if slower and continue to the next exit if you miss yours.

question: What does a red arrow pointing to the right on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Do not turn in that direction until the arrow changes to green.,b:You may turn right after coming to a complete stop.,c:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
note: A red arrow means stop for that movement; you must wait for a green arrow or green light before turning in the indicated direction.

question: Blue roadway signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas and hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage and directional distances to locations.
note: Blue signs give service information (rest areas, food, lodging, hospitals) to motorists.

question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not using a phone.,c:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks; proceed only when the crosswalk and intersection are clear.

question: With a Class C driver license you may operate which of these vehicles?
options: a:Any motor vehicle regardless of size.,b:A vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of less than 26,001 pounds.,c:A vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating over 26,001 pounds.
note: A Class C license allows operation of vehicles with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds. Larger vehicles generally require a commercial license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors, what important check should you make?
options: a:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,b:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to confirm there are no vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
