options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Use your turn signal whenever you intend to pull toward the curb or pull away so other road users understand your intentions.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness only.,b:Coordination only.,c:Both alertness and coordination.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair multiple driving skills such as alertness, coordination, judgment, and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian?
options: a:When the pedestrian is in any marked or unmarked crosswalk or crossing the street.,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when they are crossing at a signalized intersection.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and generally yield to anyone crossing the street for safety.

question: How does a BAC of 0.02 percent affect crash risk?
options: a:It can roughly double your chances of having an accident.,b:It has no effect on your driving.,c:It will not put other drivers at risk.
note: Even a small BAC increase substantially raises crash risk; each increment of alcohol impairs judgment and reaction time.

question: If visibility is less than 100 feet because of weather (rain, snow, dust, smoke, fog), what is the maximum safe speed?
options: a:30 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:40 mph.
note: If you cannot see more than 100 feet ahead, you should not drive safely faster than 30 mph due to limited sight distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never — it confuses other drivers.,b:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.,c:Often, even at controlled intersections.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield. Give up your right-of-way when doing so helps prevent a crash.

question: When will your driver's license expire?
options: a:Renew automatically.,b:Never expire.,c:On your birthday.
note: In Kansas, your driver license expires on your birthday; the Division of Vehicles will notify you before expiration with renewal instructions.

question: When you encounter orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Change lanes and keep your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce speed.,c:Maintain speed and ignore the signs.
note: As you enter a work zone, signs and message boards warn of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow or stop.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching from behind on a city street, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.,c:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down only if other cars do.
note: Yield immediately to emergency vehicles using lights and sirens by pulling to the right and stopping until they pass; clear intersections first if you are in one.

question: If smoke heavily covers the road ahead, how should you respond?
options: a:Reduce speed, move far right, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on four-way flashers and continue slowly.,c:Turn on high beams and continue.
note: Heavy smoke can be deadly; slow down, get as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway until conditions improve.

question: How can drowsiness affect driving?
options: a:Help you to be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment and performance.
note: Fatigue impairs reaction time, alertness, and judgment similar to alcohol or drugs and increases crash risk.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:So other drivers can see your vehicle.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: When precipitation or fog reduces visibility, headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see; if you use windshield wipers, low beams are required.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered railroad gate; wait until the gate is raised and you can clearly see in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, from which lane should you start the turn?
options: a:The lane in the center of the road.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane as long as it is safe.
note: Begin left turns from the far left lane on a one-way street when turning onto another one-way street to align safely with traffic flow.

question: If you must park where vehicles do not usually park, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park with your reverse lights on.
note: When parking in an unusual spot, make the vehicle as visible as possible to other road users to prevent collisions.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait for them to lift.,c:Slow down and drive around the gates.
note: Do not go around lowered gates; stop well behind them and wait until they are raised and signals stop before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you react?
options: a:Slow down and allow the other driver to return to the driving lane safely.,b:Pull off the road immediately.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When being passed in a restricted area, reduce speed and make it easy for the passing driver to move back into the lane safely.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, how should you drive?
options: a:Expect the unexpected.,b:Beep your horn to warn the child.,c:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; slow down, be prepared for sudden movements, and give them plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you look?
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Check left, then right, then left again because traffic from the left will be nearest; scan across the intersection to ensure it's clear.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, what should drivers do?
options: a:Only check the left outside mirror.,b:Look over the appropriate shoulder (left or right).,c:Only check the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors. Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to verify it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but see no gap, how should you proceed on the ramp?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for an opening.,c:Maintain your ramp speed and force drivers to yield.
note: If no space exists in freeway traffic, slow down on the ramp and wait for a safe gap so you can accelerate to traffic speed before merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left lane while many vehicles are passing you on the right and the driver behind wishes to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.,b:Stay in your lane so you don't impede traffic.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: When slower than surrounding traffic, you should move into the right lane when safe so faster drivers can pass in the left lane.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol's impairing effects from your system?
options: a:Wait.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only factor that reduces blood alcohol concentration and impairment; no food, drink, or activity will sober you faster.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicates what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only traffic beside the broken line may pass when safe to do so.

question: What is the correct approach when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and drive with extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear the zone sooner.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones present unexpected conditions; slow down and exercise heightened caution for the safety of workers and road users.

question: What should you avoid doing when passing through a construction zone?
options: a:Slowing down to watch workers or incidents (“rubbernecking”).,b:Passing carefully and remaining alert.,c:Driving with extra caution.
note: Do not slow down to look at unusual events in a work zone—rubbernecking contributes to congestion and crashes.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels and causes a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard, continuous braking on icy or snowy roads can lock wheels and make steering control impossible; brake gradually and reduce speed.

question: When the roadway is wet or icy, what action should you take?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive the posted speed.,c:Speed up to clear slippery spots.
note: Lower your speed on wet, snowy, or icy roads because tires have less traction.

question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop fully, yield, and continue only when the way is clear.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Drive closely behind the truck in bad weather because it can see farther ahead.,c:Stay about one car length behind so the truck driver can see you.
note: Maintain extra space behind trucks so you can see the road ahead and the truck driver can see you in mirrors.

question: When must vehicles stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights remain stopped?
options: a:Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,b:Until all students are off the bus.,c:Until the stop arm is retracted only.
note: Motorists must stop until the bus turns off its red lights, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven under which conditions?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed under ideal driving conditions; adjust speed lower for safety in poor conditions.

question: From top to bottom, what is the standard order of traffic signal lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, yellow, red.
note: Standard vertical traffic lights show red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are harder to see, what should drivers do?
options: a:Make frequent visual checks for motorcycles and similar vehicles.,b:Share the same lane with a motorcycle to keep it visible.,c:Slow down only when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots or missed on quick glances; drivers should continually check for them and be alert.

question: Which windows should you clear of snow, frost, and ice before driving?
options: a:All windows.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must be able to see through all windows and mirrors; remove snow, ice, and frost from all of them prior to driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it's safe to do so; always signal first.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their bright headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams and to keep enough roadway in view.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train.,b:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,c:Both of the above.
note: Even if one train passes, watch for additional trains on other tracks and do not go until all gates are up and signals have stopped.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly and slow down gradually.,b:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and apply the brakes gently when the vehicle has slowed; avoid hard or sudden braking.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what?
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem stopped for no reason.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Stop, listen, and then proceed cautiously.
note: Whenever people may cross or enter your path, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to ensure the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Do not change lanes within an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Do not make abrupt lane changes. Always signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before moving over.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking to reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When driving in fog, which lights and actions are appropriate?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights and maintain normal speed.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: Reduce speed and use low beams in fog; if visibility is extremely poor, pull over in a safe location and wait for conditions to improve.

question: Why is using a cellphone while driving distracting?
options: a:Because it occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:Because it makes the driver concern about call costs.,c:Because it draws other drivers' attention away.
note: Cellphone use while driving diverts hands, eyes, and attention from driving, increasing crash risk.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should occupants still do?
options: a:Wear seat belts at all times.,b:Not wear seat belts.,c:Wear seat belts behind the back only.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; both should be used together for maximum protection.

question: When driving in fog, which lights are best to use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect off the weather and reduce visibility.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.,b:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.
note: Always apply the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear) when parked on a hill; turn wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: If you encounter animals standing near the roadway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Swerve quickly into the next lane.
note: Animals can bolt or change direction unpredictably; reduce speed and be prepared to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely before the light changes; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,b:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds lengthen stopping distances and increase the force and severity of crashes, so reduce speed accordingly.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing mid-block instead of using a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:You must stop for them.,b:You do not have to stop for them.,c:You should honk to make them move faster.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway even if they are not using a crosswalk; avoid endangering them.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign and proceed when safe.,b:Proceed cautiously without stopping.,c:Expect the light to turn green soon.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when safe, just like a stop sign.

question: When parking uphill on a road with a curb, how should your front wheels be turned?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the steering wheel sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: Which statement best describes the mindset of defensive drivers?
options: a:They know other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating potential mistakes by others and being prepared to respond to avoid collisions.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what is the recommended way to slow the vehicle?
options: a:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.
note: Ease off the accelerator, hold the steering wheel firm, and slow gradually before steering safely off the road; avoid heavy braking until speed is reduced.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with flashing lights and its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass cautiously.
note: If a school bus has flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn. Ensure no children are crossing.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Sound your horn whenever children are present.
note: A school crossing sign warns you to be alert for children; slow down and be ready to stop as needed.

question: What should you do when prescribed a medication that may affect driving?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about its effects before driving.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Open the window and drive more slowly.
note: Ask your healthcare provider or pharmacist how a drug may affect your driving and whether it is safe to operate a vehicle.

question: When preparing to make a left turn at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:All approaching vehicles.,c:Pedestrians who have a 'Walk' signal or are in the crosswalk.
note: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles with the right-of-way, including those who have a 'Walk' signal.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs convey laws (speed, direction, parking, etc.) and are commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green text or symbols.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Using the brakes.,b:Braking lightly.,c:Braking gently and steering straight ahead.
note: If the vehicle starts to skid, do not use the brakes as braking may worsen the skid; concentrate on steering to regain control.

question: Is driving allowed while under the influence of medication that impairs driving?
options: a:No, under no circumstances.,b:Yes, if prescribed by a physician.,c:Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illicit—that impairs driving ability.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices that are obscured.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in the vehicle's mirrors; check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins skidding to the left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Not turn the steering wheel.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the right.
note: If your vehicle skids, turn the wheel in the direction of the skid to help regain control; avoid abrupt braking unless you have ABS.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, what is the best way to avoid vehicles merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic allows.,b:Slow down significantly.,c:Maintain speed and position in the right lane.
note: When safe, move out of the right-hand lane to allow merging traffic to enter from on-ramps.

question: Construction zone signs are typically what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work-zone signs are usually orange with black symbols or letters and are often diamond-shaped or rectangular.

question: What is the correct technique when backing up?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal.,c:Look through the rear window while backing up.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window while moving slowly; do not depend solely on mirrors or cameras.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, how should you re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Wait until it is safe, reduce speed, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop immediately and remain stopped.
note: Do not jerk the wheel to return. Slow, check traffic, and when safe, gradually steer back onto the pavement.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed carefully—watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:Privilege, not a right.,b:Requirement.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state that must be earned and maintained; it is not an inherent right.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you creating a hazard, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Honk and then brake firmly.,c:Swerve into the adjacent lane immediately.
note: Remove pressure from the accelerator to increase the gap to the vehicle cutting in front; avoid abrupt braking or swerving if possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Use mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror only.
note: Use mirrors and a shoulder check to see vehicles in blind spots before merging onto the freeway.

question: If dust or smoke limits your vision, what lights should you turn on?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on your headlights when conditions prevent you from seeing other vehicles; this helps others see you as well.

question: Which behavior disrupts the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Rubbernecking at collisions or unusual events slows traffic and causes congestion and secondary incidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must obey directions from officers directing traffic and come to a full stop at steady or flashing red signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,c:Passing cars.
note: Drivers making a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicycles and motorcycles, until it is safe to turn.

question: Who must drivers obey when directing traffic at a construction site?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Drivers are required to obey the instructions of flaggers in work zones, as they control traffic for safety.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can affect alertness and coordination; never drive if a drug impairs your abilities.

question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Change lanes with caution: signal, check mirrors, check blind spots, and move smoothly when safe.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: When skidding, release the accelerator or brake, steer in the direction of the skid to regain control, and avoid sudden braking.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for extended periods.,b:Follow closely to reduce wind drag.,c:Drive on its right side while on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots—don't stay beside them for long, as the driver may not see you.

question: What is the likely consequence of continually passing other cars on a two-lane road?
options: a:You will increase your chances of being in a collision.,b:You will get to your destination much more quickly and safely.,c:You will help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads increases exposure and the risk of collision, so avoid unnecessary passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:You must yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:You should slow down but never stop.
note: Approach yield signs prepared to stop and give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you intend to enter or cross if they are close enough to be a hazard.

question: If your car starts skidding out of control, what should you do with the brakes?
options: a:Stay off the brakes.,b:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Apply the brakes lightly.
note: When a vehicle is skidding, do not use the brakes; steer to regain control until the vehicle is stable and moving safely again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a green arrow, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
note: A green arrow means go but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians that remain in the intersection before turning.

question: What does a solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line allow?
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass.,b:Drivers in either direction may pass.,c:Drivers next to the solid line may pass.
note: A broken yellow beside a solid yellow allows passing for the side adjacent to the broken line only.

question: Which factor listed affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Alcohol absorption is influenced by weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and quantity consumed; weight is an important factor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single broken white lane line mean when driving on a highway?
options: a:You may cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:You cannot cross it to pass.,c:You may only cross it from the left lane.
note: Dashed white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when safe.

question: If you expect to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Applying your brakes.
note: If struck from behind, keep both hands on the wheel, press back into the seat and head restraint, and be ready to brake to avoid being pushed into another vehicle.

question: If poor weather makes it hard to see, what driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to reach your destination faster.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: In low visibility or poor weather, increase following distance to give yourself more time to react to hazards.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:You may not proceed until it turns green.,b:Treat it like a stop sign, coming to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:You are traveling in the wrong direction.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: As you approach the top of a hill, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Speed up slightly to crest the hill.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Maintain a steady speed without adjustments.
note: You may not see hazards over a hill; adjust speed so you can stop if needed for stalled vehicles or obstacles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the side of the road or the curb.,b:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parked downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's instructions and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: Traffic control instructions from a police officer override posted signals and signs; follow the officer's directions.

question: What does an instructional permit allow you to do?
options: a:Operate a motor vehicle while supervised by a licensed driver age 21 or older.,b:Operate a motor vehicle without supervision.,c:Only observe another driver operating a vehicle.
note: An instructional permit allows driving only when a licensed adult (age 21 or older) with at least one year of driving experience is seated beside you.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what speed should you maintain?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to see further.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright so others can see you.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance your headlights illuminate; high beams can blind others and should be used appropriately.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are needed to begin affecting your driving?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Alcohol affects driving ability even after a single drink; no amount of alcohol is guaranteed safe for driving.

question: You exit the freeway onto a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Wait until in the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
note: Always reduce speed before entering a curve—braking while in a curve may cause a skid and you may not see hazards ahead.

question: Which statement about drinking and driving is correct?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC means your driving is not impaired.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and skills needed to drive safely. Even small amounts can affect your ability to drive.

question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You are not required to stop if the way is clear.

question: What should you do at night regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: Reduce speed and increase following distance in darkness to allow more time to react to hazards and to avoid glare from other vehicles.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Make eye contact then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Even if no marked crosswalk exists, yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and let them finish crossing safely.

question: What color are most traffic control devices used specifically in construction and maintenance zones?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Orange.
note: Traffic control devices in work zones are typically orange to alert drivers to changed conditions and workers present.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop on its own.
note: If your vehicle has ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and let the system pump the brakes automatically for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, which should you not do?
options: a:Continue on and find another route.,b:Proceed to the next exit and return to your intended exit.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: Do not back up on the freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit and use a safe route to return.

question: Which of the following is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,b:Using your high beams in fog.,c:Staring at the road directly in front of your vehicle at all times.
note: To remain aware of the traffic around you, scan the road and check mirrors every two to five seconds; avoid using high beams in fog.

question: Which statement is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:All large trucks have air brakes that allow quick stops.
note: Large trucks require much more distance to stop than passenger cars, especially when loaded, and cannot stop as quickly.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Eating high-fat foods.
note: Only the passage of time allows your body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing else accelerates the process.

question: What message does a 'No passing zone' sign convey?
options: a:That it is not safe to pass in the indicated area.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:To speed up slightly to clear the zone.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign indicates that passing in that area is illegal because of limited visibility or other hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you take to check for other vehicles?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Before you change lanes, glance over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter to check the blind spot and confirm it is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what is required?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should always yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing a left turn. Only turn when the way is clear and signals allow.

question: Approaching a person crossing with a white cane or guide dog, what action is required?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Stop until the person is well away from your path.,c:Honk your horn as you proceed.
note: Stop and remain stopped until a blind pedestrian with a cane or guide dog has cleared your path; do not honk or attempt to pass closely.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use four-way flashers.,c:Use low beam headlights.
note: In foggy conditions use low beam headlights; high beams will reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to which of the following?
options: a:No one.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:Overtaking cars.
note: Drivers making left turns must yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight or turning right before turning left.

question: Which statement about driving slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:Driving speed does not affect safety.
note: Going much slower than surrounding traffic can create hazards by encouraging unsafe passing or backing up traffic; match the flow when safe.

question: Any concentration of alcohol acts as what type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a depressant; it slows down the central nervous system and impairs coordination, judgment, and reaction time.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Follow a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked ones.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than oncoming vehicles.
note: Choose a middle path between oncoming and parked cars to maximize clearance and reduce collision risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,b:Assume the other driver will give you room to return to your lane.,c:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
note: Never assume the space you plan to occupy is clear; only return to your lane when you can do so safely without forcing others to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what checks should you perform?
options: a:Check the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,c:Slow down and change lanes immediately.
note: Before changing lanes, check side mirrors and glance over your shoulder to confirm no vehicles are in your blind spot.

question: Which is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,b:Both tailgating other vehicles and failing to watch for workers.,c:Following another vehicle too closely (tailgating).
note: In work zones slow down, increase following distance, and be alert for workers and equipment to avoid collisions.

question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard right before the curve.
note: Slow to a safe speed before entering a curve; do most braking before the curve to reduce the chance of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer orders you to stop even though the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: Instructions from a police officer directing traffic take precedence over traffic lights, signs, or pavement markings; you must obey the officer.

question: How is a 'distraction' while driving defined?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction diverts attention from the driving task and can lead to crashes and injuries.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers have buckled theirs.,b:Buckle your safety belt only.,c:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts only.
note: Develop the habit of fastening your seat belt and confirming passengers are belted before starting the engine.

question: What can you do to help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently to remind others to yield.,c:Talk on your cell phone to stay calm while driving.
note: Signaling lane changes and turns clearly helps prevent misunderstandings and reduces the chance of conflict with other drivers.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: When following another vehicle, use low beams to avoid blinding the driver ahead and to reduce glare for both drivers.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane may not proceed in that direction.,b:You may turn after coming to a complete stop.,c:You may proceed in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane must stop and remain stopped until a green signal is displayed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at posted speed when the signal turns yellow, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is about to turn red; stop if you can safely do so, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: Which type of road surface is most likely to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses often freeze before the rest of the road because they are exposed to air on all sides.

question: When following a motorcycle, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Be ready to use your horn.,c:Allow a larger following distance (at least 3–4 seconds).
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and may fall; give them extra space, typically a three- to four-second following distance.

question: Where are truck blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the trailer.,b:Directly behind the cab only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on both sides and behind the trailer—if you can't see the driver's face in their mirror, they probably can't see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Always stop on the entrance ramp before entering.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to find a gap.
note: Use the acceleration lane to speed up, select a sufficient gap, and merge smoothly into traffic; do not stop on the ramp unless no safe gap exists.

question: When must safety belts be worn?
options: a:Only when driving long distances.,b:Do not need to be worn if airbags are present.,c:Must be worn at all times in a moving vehicle.
note: Safety belts should be worn by all occupants at all times while the vehicle is moving; they greatly reduce risk of injury.

question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Apply brakes immediately when the car starts to skid.,c:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
note: Reducing speed in wet conditions helps maintain tire contact with the road and prevents hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into highway traffic, what should you do to safely enter a gap?
options: a:Check behind you and to the side, then watch the vehicle ahead.,b:Speed up and expect other vehicles to yield.,c:Watch only the traffic behind the gap.
note: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, verify the lane you intend to enter is clear by checking mirrors and blind spots as well as the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Increase your speed to avoid causing an accident.
note: If already in the intersection when the light changes to yellow, continue through and clear it safely.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use both the lap belt and the shoulder belt.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Wear both the lap and shoulder belts together for maximum protection; using either alone reduces effectiveness.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:The number of passengers in the vehicle.,c:Driving slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden, unsafe lane changes and other risky driving maneuvers; avoid challenging them and get out of their way.

question: If approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed when clear.,c:Remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then continue when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on level roadway with no curb.
note: When parked on a slope, turn wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail; keep wheels straight when waiting to turn.

question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle carefully.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have finished crossing.,c:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.
note: You must not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield when an emergency vehicle uses siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Stop immediately, even if in an intersection.
note: Pull as far right and stop (without blocking an intersection) to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into any available lane.,b:Turn into the first (closest) lane of the one-way street.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go into the first available legal lane.

question: If the road is slippery, what following distance should you maintain?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads you need a longer distance to stop, so increase your following distance accordingly.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights; high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:When there is a broken line next to your lane.,b:When you are on a hill or curve.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.
note: You may pass where the center line is broken and passing is permitted, but never on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates what?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign only.
note: Five-sided signs typically warn of school zones or school crossings where children may be present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn not allowed?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with 500 feet clear in both directions.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians—it's too dangerous.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:No; driving too slowly can block traffic and be unsafe.,b:Yes; it is always safer to drive slower than other traffic.,c:Yes; driving slowly is a defensive driving technique in all situations.
note: While you should reduce speed in bad weather or heavy traffic, unnecessarily slow driving can impede traffic flow and be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is prohibited when changing lanes?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving laterally.

question: Which area is most likely to stay icy longer after snow or rain?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A shaded area of the road
note: Shaded areas often freeze before and thaw after other parts of the road, making them more likely to be icy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which speed should you travel at under varying conditions?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:At the speed of the vehicles immediately around you.
note: Drive at or below the legal limit and reduce speed further when road, traffic, or weather conditions make travel unsafe.

question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Slow down to no more than 10 mph.
note: If a school bus displays flashing red lights and its stop arm, you must stop and may not proceed until the signals end and the stop arm is retracted.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They increase as speed increases.,b:They are not affected by speed.,c:They decrease as speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the energy involved in a crash, raising the likelihood of serious injury or death.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When there isn't room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: Never stop on the tracks; if you cannot fully clear the crossing due to traffic or obstructions, wait until you can cross safely.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their mirrors.,c:Because large trucks travel at higher speeds than cars.
note: Large trucks and buses require more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them increase the risk of collisions.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
note: These devices warn and guide drivers away from work zone hazards to protect workers and motorists.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit.,c:Tailgate the driver in front of you.
note: Prevent aggression by focusing on driving, allowing realistic travel time, and being forgiving of others' mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: Begin your left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the lane nearest the centerline on the roadway you enter.

question: If your tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking sharply.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: Grip the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually; brake gently only if necessary and pull off when safe.

question: Where should your hands be positioned when using hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:Left hand between 7 and 8 o'clock and right hand between 4 and 5 o'clock.,b:Left hand between 9 and 10 o'clock and right hand between 2 and 3 o'clock.,c:Left hand between 10 and 11 o'clock and right hand between 1 and 2 o'clock.
note: Using push/pull steering at normal driving speeds, position your left hand around 7-8 o'clock and your right hand around 4-5 o'clock on the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight and to pedestrians crossing the roadway.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Use cruise control to hold a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions to avoid losing tire contact with the road surface (hydroplaning).

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use the horn only when necessary to avoid a collision; do not use it to express frustration or demand that others speed up.

question: Yellow pavement markings separate what?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow centerlines indicate two-way traffic; a solid yellow means no passing, while a broken yellow allows passing when it is safe.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting should you use and what should you do with speed?
options: a:Turn on high beams and speed up.,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,c:Increase speed to avoid causing an accident.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog and reduce speed. If visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution after slowing down and checking for cross traffic; a full stop is not required.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Try to fight it while driving.,b:Take a break and rest.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy, pull into a safe area and rest, nap, or change drivers rather than relying on stimulants.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited for both sides.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:In order to see potential hazards early.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways, higher speeds and faster-changing traffic require you to scan farther ahead to detect hazards and respond safely.

question: Why is driving at night generally more dangerous than during the day?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far ahead you can see at night, increasing driving risk.

question: Slowing down to look at collisions or other unusual events along the road tends to:
options: a:Cause traffic congestion.,b:Prevent rear-end collisions.,c:Improve traffic flow.
note: Rubbernecking slows traffic and contributes to congestion and secondary crashes; keep moving safely and avoid looking.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol concentration can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount of alcohol detected.
note: Kansas enforces zero tolerance for drivers under 21 — any detected alcohol can result in penalties, including a license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:When you can see the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:If you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe margin.

question: How should you view backing up your vehicle?
options: a:It is always potentially dangerous and requires caution.,b:It is dangerous only in large vehicles.,c:It is safer when a helper is present.
note: Backing up is risky because visibility is limited; use caution, check mirrors, and get assistance if needed.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can see you; use high beams only when appropriate.

question: When rain or fog reduces visibility, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog to improve your visibility and help others see you.

question: How should you adjust driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Slow down because tires have less traction than on pavement.,b:Expect better traction than on pavement.,c:Maintain normal highway speeds because visibility is the same.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance and the risk of skids; reduce speed and drive cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,b:As your speed increases, you should increase your following distance.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speeds increase the severity of crashes and require longer stopping distances, so increase following distance as speed increases.

question: When a school bus is loading or unloading children, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.
note: You must come to a complete stop whenever a school bus is loading or unloading passengers, regardless of your direction of travel.

question: What is the only proven way to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Give your body time.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Breathe in fresh air.
note: Nothing speeds elimination of alcohol from the body; only the passage of time lowers BAC and reduces impairment.

question: A broken yellow centerline means which of the following?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line indicates that passing on the left is permitted when safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: When roads are slippery after the first rain, what driving behavior is recommended?
options: a:Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.,b:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: Drive more slowly and avoid abrupt turns or stops on newly wet pavement to reduce the risk of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then merge.
note: When merging from a curb or parking, accelerate to match traffic speed and use a sufficiently large gap to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do at an intersection when the traffic control signal is not operating?
options: a:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,b:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: Treat a nonworking signal as an all-way stop: come to a complete stop and yield according to right-of-way rules before proceeding.

question: What best defines distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that makes you pay extra attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving means any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving, which increases the risk of collisions.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rain?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:If it has been raining for several hours.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Roads are most treacherous when rain first begins, as oil and dirt mix with water creating a slippery film.

question: While in a motor vehicle on a highway, what is the rule about open containers of alcohol?
options: a:It is illegal to drink from or possess open containers of alcohol.,b:It is legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.,c:It is legal to drink if you are driving but not intoxicated.
note: It is illegal for drivers or passengers to possess open containers of alcohol in a motor vehicle while it is in operation.
